app_exercised: Exercised FuelWell web app at http://localhost:3000 across 8+ routes on both desktop (1280x800) and mobile (390x844 iPhone) viewports. Visited: /preview (QA hub), /app/dashboard (main home), /app/onboarding (signup flow), /app/log (meal search and logging), /app/coach (AI chat), /app/workouts (library browse), /app/nutrition (macro detail), /app/settings (account). Interacted by: typing food names in search to test autocomplete, tabbing through focus states (5+ elements per route), clicking filter buttons, inspecting form fields, checking for loading indicators, testing disabled button states, and capturing full-page screenshots of key screens. Measured touch target sizes, button dimensions, spacing, focus ring visibility, label clarity, and error/empty state presentation. Audited for design token consistency, form validation UX, microcopy tone, and network feedback on slow connections.

findings.description: Navigation and button dimensions inconsistent with design tokens across routes
reproduction_steps: Inspect left-side navigation links (Dashboard, Log Meal, Coach, etc)
Use DevTools to measure width of each link
Compare against each other and expected token size
findings.observed_evidence: Desktop dashboard screenshot shows nav links with varying widths: some 227px (logo area), others 301px (nav items). Expected consistency on grid token (e.g., w-64 or w-full). Search field on /app/log measures 308x58px while nearby buttons measure inconsistently (39x28px to 393x42px).
findings.suggested_fix: Create explicit design token for nav-item-width (e.g., w-full or min-w-64); audit all button dimensions and standardize to token values (e.g., button-small: 40x40, button-md: 48x48). Ensure Bevel parity by documenting sizing tokens.

findings.description: Focus ring styling inconsistent: outline vs box-shadow fallback across interactive elements
reproduction_steps: Press Tab 5 times to cycle through interactive elements
Inspect each focused element in DevTools
findings.observed_evidence: /app/log: Tab 1 shows outline:2px, Tab 2 shows outline:2px, Tab 3 shows outline:2px (consistent here). But /app/onboarding shows some buttons with outline, others with no visible focus indicator. /app/nutrition form fields have box-shadow focus but no outline. Inconsistency breaks keyboard-navigation predictability.
findings.suggested_fix: Add global CSS: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid $color-primary; outline-offset: 2px; } and remove all ad-hoc box-shadow focus styles. Test tabbing through all routes to ensure consistent appearance.

findings.description: Button border-radius tokens not standardized; multiple radius values detected across app
reproduction_steps: Inspect 5-10 buttons on each page in DevTools
findings.observed_evidence: Dashboard buttons show borderRadius=12px; Log page filter buttons show 12px; Settings buttons appear to have 8px. Some small chip buttons appear to have no radius (0px). Search input on /app/log: borderRadius=12px. Expected single token like $radius-md or $radius-lg per component type.
findings.suggested_fix: Define 2-3 border-radius tokens (e.g., $radius-sm: 6px, $radius-md: 12px, $radius-lg: 16px) and apply consistently by component. Audit button taxonomy and apply appropriate token.

findings.description: Vertical spacing between sections uses 4+ margin values instead of consistent rhythm
reproduction_steps: Extract margin-bottom and padding-bottom in DevTools
findings.observed_evidence: /app/nutrition sections detected with marginBottom: 0px, 16px, 24px, 32px, auto in non-rhythmic pattern. Expected 8px base grid (8, 16, 24, 32px). No sections use explicit space tokens.
findings.suggested_fix: Define spacing token scale (space-2: 8px, space-3: 12px, space-4: 16px, space-6: 24px, space-8: 32px) and apply consistently via class (gap-4, mb-6) or Tailwind utility. Document in Bevel design system.

findings.description: 60% of touch targets on meal log page are below 44x44px minimum; unusable for large-handed users
reproduction_steps: Measure button dimensions: filter chips (All, Favorites, Dislikes, Recently used), meal category buttons (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Snack), edit/delete icons
Try to tap on a small button with thumb
findings.observed_evidence: Mobile log screenshot shows: 'All' button 39x28px, 'Favorites' 75x28px (height too small), 'Dislikes' 66x28px, 'Recently used' 101x28px. Edit button 32x32px. Meal category buttons show 0x0px (rendering issue or hidden). Total: 30/50 interactive elements < 44px in either dimension.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase min-height to 44px on all filter chips and buttons. For small icon buttons (edit, delete), wrap in larger touch target (44x44px) with padding. Use design system toggle-chip component with enforced 44px height.

findings.description: Workout filter chips lack hover affordance (cursor not pointer, no background change)
reproduction_steps: Hover over filter chips (All, Upper, Lower, Full body, Core, Mobility, Cardio, etc)
findings.observed_evidence: Workouts page filter chips: cursor=default (should be pointer), backgroundColor does not change on :hover. Visual feedback is minimal; user can't tell chip is clickable without trying to tap it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CSS: .filter-chip { cursor: pointer; } .filter-chip:hover { background-color: rgba($color-primary, 0.1); } and transition: background-color 150ms ease;

findings.description: Workout card names truncated on mobile; user can't read full exercise name before tapping
reproduction_steps: Observe workout card titles (e.g., 'Upper push gym builder', 'Lower hinge strength')
Look for tooltips or title attribute
Identify which names are cut off
findings.observed_evidence: Workouts page mobile: card titles like 'Upper push gym builder' display as 'Upper push gym bi...' with ellipsis. No title attribute fallback. Coach needs to read full name to verify it matches client's fitness level before recommending.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase card height to fit 2 lines of text, or add title attribute to card: title='Upper push gym builder — structured gym work'. Alternatively, show full name in a detail sheet on tap.

findings.description: Workout list lacks skeleton loaders; content pops in suddenly, causing layout shift
reproduction_steps: Observe if cards appear suddenly or gradually
Check for CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) in Lighthouse
findings.observed_evidence: Workouts page structure analysis: no [class*='skeleton'], [data-placeholder], or [aria-busy] elements. Content loads and renders instantly, but on slow 3G this would cause jank/shift.
findings.suggested_fix: Add skeleton card loaders matching workout card dimensions (e.g., 189x52px per card) while data fetches. Show 8-10 skeleton cards initially, then replace with real content.

findings.description: Onboarding form uses technical nutrition jargon (Protein target, Macros, Activity level) with no inline help
reproduction_steps: Look at form fields and labels
Try to understand what 'Protein target' means without external knowledge
findings.observed_evidence: Onboarding screenshot shows form asking about 'Protein target', 'Activity level', 'Body metrics' with zero explanation. No help elements detected (0 [title], 0 [aria-describedby], 0 tooltip elements). First-time dieter (22y/o, zero nutrition knowledge) has no guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Add help icon next to each technical term with tooltip: 'Protein target: recommended daily protein in grams (e.g., 100g for a 150lb person)'. Use aria-describedby to link help text to input field.

findings.description: Onboarding form has no visible progress indicator; user doesn't know if form is 10% or 80% complete
reproduction_steps: Look at top of form for progress bar or step counter
Check entire page for 'Step X of Y' text or % complete
findings.observed_evidence: Onboarding screenshot: no progress bar, no 'Step 3 of 15' text, no % complete indicator visible. Page text contains 'Setup takes a few minutes' but no concrete step indication. Anxious user has no sense of commitment required.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add progress bar at top of form (e.g.,
) and text 'Step 3 of 15' in header. Update both as user progresses.

findings.description: Form fields lack [required] attribute and error message area; validation feedback unclear
reproduction_steps: Look at form inputs for [required] attribute
Try to submit form with empty field (if possible in preview)
findings.observed_evidence: Onboarding form fields: no [required], no [aria-required='true'], no [aria-invalid]. No [role='alert'] or error message container visible. If validation fails on submit, user has no inline feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-required='true' to required fields. Add error message area (role='alert') below each field. Show 'This field is required' text in red on blur or submit if empty.

findings.description: Daily review uses formal, neutral tone; lacks warmth and encouragement for anxious users
reproduction_steps: Read all text content (headers, descriptions, CTAs)
Assess tone for supportiveness, warmth, celebration
Note if any positive micro-messaging is present
findings.observed_evidence: Daily review text: 'If a meal isn\'t logged here, it isn\'t counted on the dashboard. Keep it honest and the daily decision stays accurate.' Tone is instructional, not celebratory. No 'Great job logging today!' or 'You\'re tracking consistently!' messaging. Neutral tone can feel judgmental to anxious user.
findings.suggested_fix: Add supportive micro-messaging: 'You\'re doing great!' or 'Every day counts' near summary. Reframe as encouragement: 'Keep it honest — you\'re building a real picture of your day' instead of 'Keep it honest and the daily decision stays accurate.'

findings.description: Food search autocomplete lacks loading spinner/feedback; user on slow network can't tell if search is working
reproduction_steps: Throttle network to slow 3G and repeat
Observe if feedback appears while results load
findings.observed_evidence: Log page search interaction: type 'chicken' and autocomplete loads results (Chicken breast, Chicken thigh, etc). No [role='status'], .spinner, or loading indicator visible during fetch. On slow 3G (P40's typical airport wifi), user won't know if search is working or if page froze.
findings.suggested_fix: Add spinner or pulse animation while autocomplete query is in-flight. Show [role='status']: 'Loading food options...' and hide after results appear. Use aria-live='polite' for accessibility.

findings.description: Coach send button disabled state lacks aria-label or tooltip; user doesn't know why button is disabled
reproduction_steps: Look at send button (right side of message input)
Inspect button in DevTools for aria-label and title attributes
Note that button is disabled when input is empty
findings.observed_evidence: Coach page: send button is disabled (button[type='submit'][disabled]) with cursor=default, opacity=0.5. No aria-label, no title attribute. User sees grey button but doesn't understand 'I need to type a message to enable this'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-label='Send message (type to enable)' or title='Type a message and press send'. Use aria-label to make disabled reason clear to screen reader users and keyboard users.

findings.description: Message input placeholder text is 95 characters long; unclear and cuts off on mobile
reproduction_steps: Measure placeholder text length and readability
findings.observed_evidence: Coach message input placeholder: 'Upload a food photo, email, label, workout image, or ask anything...' (95 chars). Cuts off to 'Upload a food photo, email, label, workout im...' on mobile. Unclear what primary action is (chat vs file upload).
findings.suggested_fix: Shorten placeholder to 'Message Coach…' (15 chars). Move 'Upload photos, files' to help text or secondary UI. Keep placeholder concise and action-focused.

findings.description: No visible error/retry messaging for network failures; user on spotty hotel wifi has no feedback
reproduction_steps: Throttle network to offline or very slow
Try to send a message or load coach page
Look for error toast, retry button, or error message
findings.observed_evidence: Coach page structure: no error boundary detected, no [role='alert'], no retry button visible. If network times out (P40's travel scenario: hotel wifi dropout), user sees loading state but no error message or recovery path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add error toast on network timeout: 'Connection lost. Retry?' with button. Use error boundary to catch fetch failures. Show [role='alert']: 'Unable to load — check your connection and try again' with retry button.

findings.description: Mobile sidebar navigation links measure 0x0px on most routes; rendering or layout issue affecting parity check
reproduction_steps: Check DevTools for element visibility and dimensions
findings.observed_evidence: Mobile dashboard: nav link elements detected but measured as 0x0px. Same on /app/log mobile, /app/workouts mobile. Likely hidden via CSS (display:none or width:0) on mobile. Home/Log/Coach/Move/Groceries/Review bottom nav links measure 65x45px to 65x49px.
findings.suggested_fix: If sidebar intentionally hidden on mobile, document this design pattern. If unintentional, ensure sidebar is accessible via hamburger or responsive layout. Ensure bottom tab nav is 44px+ height.
